nodes.text: Morning drill begins with a staged report from the outbound warehouse floor.
nodes.speaker: Coordinator

nodes.text: The observer sees thin gray smoke drifting above the charging station.
nodes.speaker: Spotter

nodes.text: The observer is clear of the hazard and can continue reporting from a safe point.
nodes.speaker: Coordinator

nodes.text: The shift lead acknowledges the report and asks for a location update.
nodes.speaker: ShiftLead

nodes.text: The fire team stages outside the aisle and waits for severity classification.
nodes.speaker: FireMarshal

nodes.text: Two chargers are active and one bay shows a blinking fault light.
nodes.speaker: Spotter

nodes.text: A solvent drum is weeping under the lower rim and liquid is pooling toward the conveyor.
nodes.speaker: Spotter

nodes.text: The label confirms a flammable cleaning solvent with a low flash point.
nodes.speaker: Coordinator

nodes.text: The absorbent barrier slows the spread and keeps liquid out of the walking lane.
nodes.speaker: SafetyLead

nodes.text: The hazmat coordinator requests a severity rating before dispatching the spill team.
nodes.speaker: HazmatDesk

nodes.text: Packing lane two is paused so no cartons pass through the spill zone.
nodes.speaker: WarehouseOps

nodes.text: A pallet on the fourth level is leaning forward and one beam looks twisted.
nodes.speaker: Spotter

nodes.text: Tape and cones block the aisle so no picker enters the unstable bay.
nodes.speaker: SafetyLead

nodes.text: The inspection finds scrape marks on the upright and one loose pallet board.
nodes.speaker: Coordinator

nodes.text: Maintenance logs the rack location and waits for the triage result.
nodes.speaker: MaintenanceLead

nodes.text: Pickers are reassigned to the overflow lane to keep the drill moving safely.
nodes.speaker: WarehouseOps

nodes.text: A worker is seated on the floor after a shrink-wrap cart clipped the shin guard.
nodes.speaker: Spotter

nodes.text: The first-aid lead is en route and asks whether there is visible bleeding.
nodes.speaker: MedicLead

nodes.text: Nearby forklift traffic is frozen and the crossing lane is held clear.
nodes.speaker: WarehouseOps

nodes.text: Two witnesses confirm the cart entered the crossing before the spotter called stop.
nodes.speaker: Coordinator

nodes.text: The worker can stand with assistance but reports sharp pain when turning.
nodes.speaker: Spotter

nodes.text: The strobe and siren are active, but the camera feed shows no obvious smoke or spill.
nodes.speaker: ControlRoom

nodes.text: The last reset happened during battery maintenance one hour ago.
nodes.speaker: Coordinator

nodes.text: The panel points to a detector above the charging cages and no other zones are active.
nodes.speaker: ControlRoom

nodes.text: The sweep finds a warm charger housing that may explain the alarm.
nodes.speaker: Spotter

nodes.text: A draft closeout form is opened in case the drill is ruled a false alarm.
nodes.speaker: Coordinator

nodes.text: The observation report now includes location, people affected, active controls, and reporting notes.
nodes.speaker: Coordinator

nodes.text: Low-impact events stay local, but the team still has to assign a documented control.
nodes.speaker: SafetyLead

nodes.text: A spotter remains in place and logs every movement through the zone.
nodes.speaker: SafetyLead

nodes.text: Only the affected lane is paused while neighboring work continues under watch.
nodes.speaker: WarehouseOps

nodes.text: Limited-area events require a perimeter, an operations hold, and recovery planning.
nodes.speaker: OpsLead

nodes.text: The perimeter now covers the aisle, the adjacent dock door, and the cross-lane walkway.
nodes.speaker: OpsLead

nodes.text: Outgoing pallets from the affected zone are marked on hold in the queue.
nodes.speaker: InventoryControl

nodes.text: A vendor call tree is opened, but dispatch waits for the final recovery decision.
nodes.speaker: OpsLead

nodes.text: Site-level emergencies shift to incident command and coordinated notifications.
nodes.speaker: SiteLead

nodes.text: Emergency services are notified in the drill timeline and staging instructions are announced.
nodes.speaker: SiteLead

nodes.text: Bays one through four are cleared and dock traffic is rerouted to the north apron.
nodes.speaker: SecurityDesk

nodes.text: The radio bridge opens for site lead, safety, security, and floor operations.
nodes.speaker: ControlRoom

nodes.text: False-alarm cases still need documentation before operations can fully reopen.
nodes.speaker: Coordinator

nodes.text: The detector is reset and a watch period begins for the charging zone.
nodes.speaker: ControlRoom

nodes.text: The alarm ticket is closed with drill annotations and the trigger source.
nodes.speaker: ControlRoom

nodes.text: The false-alarm packet is complete and no active hazard remains on the floor.
nodes.speaker: Coordinator

nodes.text: The drill closes as a documented false alarm and normal work can continue.
nodes.speaker: Coordinator

nodes.text: Cleanup and recovery tasks are assigned before any restart decision is approved.
nodes.speaker: SafetyLead

nodes.text: Floor leads receive the restart estimate and revised work assignments.
nodes.speaker: WarehouseOps

nodes.text: HR logs the drill timing and any injury simulation notes for training records.
nodes.speaker: HRDesk

nodes.text: Leadership receives the severity summary, control actions, and recovery timing.
nodes.speaker: SiteLead

nodes.text: Security confirms dock doors and pedestrian gates remain under the drill perimeter rules.
nodes.speaker: SecurityDesk

nodes.text: The recovery checklist tracks cleanup, briefing, and restart prerequisites.
nodes.speaker: Coordinator

nodes.text: The area is clean, tagged, and ready for restart authorization.
nodes.speaker: OpsLead

nodes.text: Team members sign the post-drill briefing sheet and acknowledge next steps.
nodes.speaker: SafetyLead

nodes.text: Lessons learned are logged and action items are assigned to named owners.
nodes.speaker: Coordinator

nodes.text: Open questions remain, so the drill is handed to the investigation queue.
nodes.speaker: SiteLead

nodes.text: The event remains closed for operations until the investigation report is reviewed.
nodes.speaker: SiteLead

nodes.text: The drill is complete and the warehouse returns to standard monitoring.
nodes.speaker: Coordinator

nodes.text: Normal picking waves resume with spot checks for the next shift.
nodes.speaker: OpsLead

nodes.text: Manual packing restarts first while the affected equipment remains locked out.
nodes.speaker: OpsLead

edges.text: 1. [Observe: Smoke] Report light haze near the battery charging cages.
2. [Observe: Spill] Report a leaking solvent drum beside packing lane two.
3. [Observe: Rack] Report a leaning pallet stack in high-bay storage.
4. [Observe: Injury] Report a worker clipped by a shrink-wrap cart.
5. [Observe: Alarm] Report a flashing siren without an obvious hazard.
1. Move the observer to a safe point near the fire cabinet.
2. [Notify: Shift Lead] Call the shift lead to bay three.
3. [Escalate: Fire Team] Request extinguisher team standby.
4. Check whether batteries are currently charging.
1. Read the drum label before anyone moves it.
2. Deploy absorbent socks around the pooling liquid.
3. [Notify: Hazmat Coordinator] Call the hazmat desk for guidance.
4. Stop the conveyor on packing lane two.
1. Cordon the rack aisle immediately.
2. Inspect nearby beams for bend marks.
3. [Notify: Maintenance] Request a structural check from maintenance.
4. Move nearby pickers to the overflow lane.
1. [Notify: Medic] Call the first-aid lead to the scene.
2. Freeze nearby forklift traffic.
3. Record witness statements while the lane is quiet.
4. Check whether the worker can walk without support.
1. Check the last detector reset log.
2. [Notify: Control Room] Confirm which panel triggered the alarm.
3. Sweep the zone for a hidden heat source.
4. Prepare a false-alarm closeout packet.
1. Classify the inject as low impact.
2. Classify the event as limited-area disruption.
3. [Escalate: Site Lead] Classify the event as a site-level emergency.
4. Classify the event as a likely false alarm.
1. Keep the zone open with a spotter posted.
2. Pause only the affected lane while checks finish.
3. Route the low-severity case into cleanup planning.
1. Expand the perimeter and halt local picking.
2. [Notify: Inventory Control] Hold outgoing pallets from the zone.
3. Prepare external vendor support if the condition worsens.
4. Route the limited-area case into cleanup planning.
1. [Escalate: 911] Simulate emergency services notification.
2. Order full evacuation of bays one through four.
3. Activate the incident command radio bridge.
4. Route the site-level case into cleanup planning.
1. Reset the detector and document the cause.
2. [Notify: Control Room] Close the alarm ticket with drill notes.
3. Reopen operations after a final sweep.
4. Route the false-alarm case into cleanup planning.
1. [Notify: Warehouse Ops] Send the restart estimate to floor leads.
2. [Notify: HR] Log injury and drill timing details for training review.
3. [Notify: Site Lead] Send the severity summary to leadership.
4. [Notify: Security Desk] Confirm dock doors remain controlled.
5. Move directly to the recovery checklist.
1. Verify the area is clean and equipment is tagged.
2. Confirm the staff briefing is complete.
3. [Wrap-Up] Hold the final debrief before restart.
4. [Wrap-Up] Escalate unresolved issues to investigation.
1. Resume normal picking waves.
2. Reopen only manual packing stations.
3. Keep the zone closed pending investigation.
